title: Home Automation
searchIntent: grok bot to run my smart home
intro: This is the category people did not predict and it is larger than several of the business ones: bots that watch a house. Charging schedules against electricity rates, network health, deliveries, thermostats, the robot vacuum. What makes it work is that a home produces a steady stream of small numbers nobody is watching, which is exactly the gap an always-on agent fills. The listings are highly personal — most were built for one house and shared afterwards — so expect to rewrite the specifics rather than install and go. The interesting design question is how much the bot is allowed to actuate. A bot that reports the tumble dryer finished is uncontroversial. A bot that changes the thermostat because electricity got cheap is making a decision on behalf of everyone in the building, which is worth agreeing with them first.

bots.fitReason: Purpose-built house mission control: Tesla charging against electricity rates, Starlink/ISP health, home devices, surfaced in priority order. Written for one specific house, in Chinese, so expect to rewrite every device and tariff before it means anything to yours.

Actually actuates: connect a Navimow mower, a Matic vacuum or Matter robots once, then command them from chat. Only covers robots — no thermostats, energy or network — and you are handing a bot the keys to machines that move around your garden.

Watches a home EG4 hybrid solar and battery setup, pulls production, storage and grid figures, archives charts and flags faults — exactly the stream of small numbers nobody checks. Read-only and useless unless you own EG4 kit.

Builds and maintains a TRMNL plugin that puts UniFi Protect air-quality sensor readings on a screen, via a LAN poller and webhook. A genuine piece of home telemetry plumbing, but it is one sensor on one dashboard, not a house-wide agent.
